answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation expensive to earn and worthless to fake: each identity must build a verifiable history of completed, useful work before it can join high-value trades. A newcomer is an uncut onyx, unproven and limited to small tasks. Consistent delivery earns it the shifting facets of an opal, a public record peers can check. Only sustained good conduct over time earns pearl status. Spinning up a thousand fakes gains nothing, because every fake starts at zero and must pay the same slow cost to climb.
